thread:
incident-bot: @here P1 detected on /v1/generate — elevated 5xx and token latency starting ~2026-03-15T12:03:00Z. Autoscaler (HPA) is oscillating, GPU pool shows saturation + long warmup tails. Paging eng-oncall.

lee_oncall: Acknowledged. I’m grabbing metrics now. Can folks paste any recent hpa/k8s outputs and queue depths? We need a timeline and immediate mitigations.

marie_sre: Seen a big spike in queue depth at 12:02, sustained until ~12:12. Customer error rate ~18% for hosted v1. I have CloudWatch/Prometheus graphs; attaching snippet below.

nora_eng: Quick hypothesis: HPA scaled down too aggressively last night -> minReplicas too low for bursty traffic -> new requests hit cold workers and wait for GPU allocations + model warmup. That would cause queue pile-up and higher tail latency.

alex_ml: Also seeing high KV cache miss ratio during the incident window — warmup not hitting cache. Could be model variant swap or evicted caches due to memory pressure.

lee_oncall: Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n infra get hpa inference-hpa -o wide
# Output (sample):
NAME            REFERENCE               TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-hpa   Deployment/inference    120%/80%  1         20        1          3d
```
and
```
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=inference -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.metadata.creationTimestamp}\n{end}'
```
Pods show lots of restart/warmup timestamps clustered at 12:03-12:05.

samir_support: Customer-impact numbers: approx 6k requests failed with 5xx between 12:03–12:12 (~0.6% of daily traffic for US hosted). Critical flows (interactive chat) got higher latency, support queue spiked. I’ll draft an incident note for customers once we have a mitigation summary.

lee_oncall: Live mitigation checklist (doing in parallel):
- Increase HPA minReplicas to 4 temporarily -> marie, can you push?
- Evict long-running batch jobs on gpu-pool to free nodes -> nora, coordinate with batch team.
- Promote fallback model-quantized variant with faster warmup for hosted tier -> alex, can you gate?
- Adjust prewarm policy to add 2 standby workers in busy regions -> I’ll open a quick config change.

marie_sre: Pushed HPA change to minReplicas=4. Watchers, expect additional pods to show up in ~30–90s. Patch: kubectl apply -f hpa-temp-min4.yaml.

nora_eng: Requeued/evicted two batch jobs from gpu-pool, freed 3 GPUs. Scheduling shows pods now pending->running.

alex_ml: Can push model fallback. Deploying quantized-small variant as /v1/generate-fallback; adding routing rule to divert 30% traffic. Minimal quality change but much faster warmup.

oncall-bot: Deploy event: model-fallback promoted to 30% traffic at 12:07:45Z — rollout started.

lee_oncall: Good. Early signs: queue depth dropped ~65% by 12:09, error rate down to 3% by 12:10. Still seeing a few long-tail 5xx from warmup failures.

alex_ml: Sharing logs for a failed warmup attempt (sanitized):
```
[12:03:14Z] WARN model_warmup: load_timeout=45s, gpu_allocate_delay=12s
[12:03:26Z] ERROR inference: kernel_init_failed: cuda-malloc OOM on 0x7f
[12:03:27Z] INFO fallback: routing user -> quantized-small
```
Hypothesis H1: OOMs during kernel init from memory pressure causing warmup to fail and HPA to see high CPU -> scale decisions oscillate.

marie_sre: Hypothesis H2: HPA target metric is request-per-second on the front proxy; proxy sees TTL spikes and bursts due to caching misses, so HPA overshoots/undershoots. Need to correlate with proxy metrics at 12:02–12:06.

lee_oncall: Agreed. I'll tag H1 and H2 in the incident doc and ask infra to dump kube-scheduler events and node allocatable mem for 12:00–12:10.

nora_eng: Scheduler events show a backlog at 12:03 due to GPU resource fragmentation — several nodes had <1 GPU free which prevented packing. That's consistent with slow allocation.

samir_support: For handoff: customers impacted, mitigation in place (HPA minReplicas increased, batch evictions, fallback model routing). Suggested next steps for RCA: correlate warmup OOMs with node memory pressure, evaluate HPA metric (use queue depth or a custom GPU-util metric), and consider adding prewarming pool.

lee_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @marie_sre — leaving notes: incident entered mitigation state at 12:10Z, partial rollback not needed, fallback still routing 30%, monitor error rate <1% goal. Please continue timeline enrichment and pull scheduler/node logs.

marie_sre: Taking over. Will collect kube-scheduler events, node metrics, and full request traces. I’ll update incident doc with a preliminary timeline and assign to infra/serving for RCA.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by marie_sre. Severity remains P1 until error rate <1% for 15m window.

lee_oncall: Final note before I sign off: primary shortfall appears to be combined: aggressive scaling policy + GPU fragmentation + memory pressure during warmup. Candidate remediations to include in RCA: increase minReplicas for burst safety, change HPA signal to include GPU-alloc/pending queue, introduce small warm pool per-region, and tune eviction/packing strategy on gpu nodes.

marie_sre: Copy. Will schedule RCA sync tomorrow and post action items. :thumbsup:
